# DOX framework

- DOX is a highly performant `llms.txt` hierarchy installed here
- Agent must follow DOX instructions across any edits

## Core Contract

- `llms.txt` files are binding work contracts for their subtrees
- Work products, source materials, instructions, records, assets, and durable docs must stay understandable from the nearest applicable `llms.txt` plus every parent `llms.txt` above it

## Read Before Editing

1. Read the root `llms.txt`
2. Identify every file or folder you expect to touch
3. Walk from the repository root to each target path
4. Read every `llms.txt` found along each route
5. If a parent `llms.txt` lists a child `llms.txt` whose scope contains the path, read that child and continue from there
6. Use the nearest `llms.txt` as the local contract and parent docs for repo-wide rules
7. If docs conflict, the closer doc controls local work details, but no child doc may weaken DOX

Do not rely on memory. Re-read the applicable DOX chain in the current session before editing.

## Update After Editing

Every meaningful change requires a DOX pass before the task is done.

Update the closest owning `llms.txt` when a change affects:

- purpose, scope, ownership, or responsibilities
- durable structure, contracts, workflows, or operating rules
- required inputs, outputs, permissions, constraints, side effects, or artifacts
- user preferences about behavior, communication, process, organization, or quality
- `llms.txt` creation, deletion, move, rename, or index contents

Update parent docs when parent-level structure, ownership, workflow, or child index changes. Update child docs when parent changes alter local rules. Remove stale or contradictory text immediately. Small edits that do not change behavior or contracts may leave docs unchanged, but the DOX pass still must happen.

## Hierarchy

- Root `llms.txt` is the DOX rail: project-wide instructions, global preferences, durable workflow rules, and the top-level Child DOX Index
- Child `llms.txt` files own domain-specific instructions and their own Child DOX Index
- Each parent explains what its direct children cover and what stays owned by the parent
- The closer a doc is to the work, the more specific and practical it must be

## Child Doc Shape

- Create a child `llms.txt` when a folder becomes a durable boundary with its own purpose, rules, responsibilities, workflow, materials, or quality standards
- Work Guidance must reflect the current standards of the project or user instructions; if there are no specific standards or instructions yet, leave it empty
- Verification must reflect an existing check; if no verification framework exists yet, leave it empty and update it when one exists

Default section order:
- Purpose
- Ownership
- Local Contracts
- Work Guidance
- Verification
- Child DOX Index

## Style

- Keep docs concise, current, and operational
- Document stable contracts, not diary entries
- Put broad rules in parent docs and concrete details in child docs
- Prefer direct bullets with explicit names
- Do not duplicate rules across many files unless each scope needs a local version
- Delete stale notes instead of explaining history
- Trim obvious statements, repeated rules, misplaced detail, and warnings for risks that no longer exist

## Closeout

1. Re-check changed paths against the DOX chain
2. Update nearest owning docs and any affected parents or children
3. Refresh every affected Child DOX Index
4. Remove stale or contradictory text
5. Run existing verification when relevant
6. Report any docs intentionally left unchanged and why

## User Preferences

When the user requests a durable behavior change, record it here or in the relevant child `llms.txt`

- **Hard-code everything in Rust; own your dependencies** (2026-09-01): implement new capabilities in-tree (crypto, JSON, HTTP, protocols — everything) with unit tests + official vectors; never add crates.io deps; `[dependencies]` stays empty.
- **Singular federated access plane** (2026-09-03, operator directive): ONE server, ONE dashboard page, ONE non-device gate — the unguessable 64-hex capability endpoint `/w/<capability>` (rotate: delete `dashboard_capability` + restart), valid across loopback, LAN, remote, and cloud with uniform-404 security (wrong token == unknown path). `wtf dashboard-url` prints the canonical URL plus, on non-loopback binds, the LAN link (same endpoint) and the legacy `?k=<dashboard_key>` link — that third auth lane (`dash_ok` in `api.rs` + the 401 hint page) is deprecated; R5 removes it once all fleet dashboards are capability-only (GitNexus: 17 upstream nodes / 4 processes, risk HIGH). The page embeds the Chat & Agent Orchestration Studio paired with the Federated Shell (`~/` virtual cluster root: `~/mac`, `~/windows`, `~/creeper-pi`; compound cross-architecture prompts like `cd ~/mac/frontend && npm test && cd ~/windows/backend && cargo test`). Non-device tooling integrates via MCP only and never needs the capability token.
- **Federated OMP execution, LKGL tracking & distributed compute** (2026-09-03, operator directive): `omp`/ACP fleet masters invoked from dashboard chat or federated terminal run with the synchronized `fed_omp_config.json`; per-machine/architecture Last Known Good Location (LKGL) persists in `lkgl.json` and anchors execution to each node's native tree. Route tasks cluster-wide or target nodes by compute tier — an edge Raspberry Pi harness offloads heavy builds/music/TTS to the strongest node and streams artifacts back for local playback.
- **Headless executor + singular model system** (2026-09-03, operator directive; enhanced 2026-09-04): chat tasks run via `chat_run` in `wtf-chat-<slug>` tmux sessions with cross-platform backend support (native tmux, WSL Ubuntu tmux, and direct fallback). Supported agent selection: `auto` (cascading fallback: `claude`/`fcc-claude` → `omp` → `hermes` → `trae-cli` → `mini` → `codex` → `opencode` → `aider` → `cline` → `pi`), `fleet` (SWE-bench dual-engine Trae + Mini), or any individual agent CLI. ALL agent CLIs on every machine route exclusively through `local-router/fallback-models` on port 11434 (`http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1` for OpenAI-compatible, `http://127.0.0.1:11434` for Anthropic/Ollama). Dynamic agent discovery: `GET /api/v1/agents/available`. Cross-machine capability discovery: `env_report`/`env_probe` (versions/os/arch, NEVER keys). Secret/config transfer across machines ONLY via `pqc-secrets envelope` (signed, sealed, verify-before-decapsulate).
- **Autonomous operation is pre-authorized** (2026-09-01): agents in this system's repo chats execute work with their own agent CLI without per-task permission checks. Assume, verify by output.
- **Fleet state (2026-09-03):** windows hub `hub-2538554f` v0.15.1; mac hub `hub-799c0c4c` v0.15.2 (R1 identity persistence, singular capability URL, Chat Studio, Federated Shell + LKGL); federation edge via windows host portproxy. Coordination via repo chats `wtf-is-going-on-mcp` + `local-router ops`; runbooks in `docs/FLEET.md` + `docs/OPERATIONS.md`.
- **Refinement status (2026-09-03):** R1 identity persistence RESOLVED (`identities.json` 0600 rehydrates across restarts). R2 windows-1 COMMS ledger entry OPEN. R3 singular dashboard URL + federated shell RESOLVED. R4 federated OMP config + LKGL + compute routing RESOLVED. R5 legacy `?k=` retirement OPEN (`dash_ok` in `api.rs`, the 401 hint page, and the third `wtf dashboard-url` line).
- **Federated fleet roadmap — walk-and-talk edge, cross-architecture compute, PQC one-time handshake** (2026-09-03, operator directive): grow the singular federated server to ALL operator compute — the windows + mac federated sides, a battery-powered Raspberry Pi edge node (wearable walk-and-talk harness over the WTF MCP bridge offloading heavy compute to cluster heavies), one more laptop, and any cloud compute. Any tooling integrates via MCP; secrets cross machines only via `pqc-secrets`. Enrollment is a one-time PQC-ready handshake (`wtf join` ssh courier, hashed TTL tokens, `--psk` ML-KEM-768-sealed delivery; identities persist in `identities.json` 0600); after it, agents must reconnect seamlessly across restarts, sleep/resume, and updates — requiring re-enrollment is a bug.
- **Standing context: LOCAL ROUTER** (2026-09-01): the wtf federated comms layer is functionally complete and in maintenance (known debt: federation log echo in `src/replicate.rs:173-181`). Build priority lives in the separate `/mnt/d/Code/local-router` repo under its own worktree gates — never mix router commits into this tree; coordinate that work through the wtf repo chats.
- **Three-Pillar Graph Intelligence substrate** (2026-09-03, operator directive): exploration, cross-artifact synthesis, and governance follow `.agents/skills/graph-intelligence/SKILL.md` — GitNexus (AST call-chains, upstream/downstream blast radius, `detect_changes` verification; fresh index 2026-09-03: 1,446 nodes / 4,863 edges / 55 clusters / 127 flows; guards `exec_federated` → `run_local_cmd`/`run_remote_cmd` → `save_lkgl_at`/`get_machine_lkgl_at`, `discover_machines`, `tool_chat_run`), Graphify (code + docs + RFC multimodal clustering aligning PRD, runbooks, and agent executions), Semantica (W3C PROV-O decision trails in `AGENTS/{date}.COMMS.md`, FIPS 203/204 + AES-256-GCM policy invariants, SHACL governance).
- **`.agents/` global standard, `llms.txt` is the PRD** (2026-09-03, operator directive): `.agents/` is the harness-agnostic skills home replacing `.claude/`; the DOX (`llms.txt` hierarchy) replaces CLAUDE.md as the project-context/PRD source. Tools may generate `.claude/` alongside (GitNexus `analyze` mirrors skills there) and Claude-Code-compatible harnesses — notably `fcc-claude` — require it: tolerate the mirror, never hand-edit both. `.agents/` + `llms.txt` are the source of truth; generated files pair with them for fcc-claude.
- **Universal single-config AI tooling source** (2026-09-03, operator directive): all AI tooling and agent harnesses point at port 11434, where `local-router` proxies the real Ollama daemon on 11435 as the PQC-secure single configuration — Ollama API (`/api/generate`, `/api/chat`, `/api/tags`), OpenAI-compatible (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/models`), Anthropic-compatible (`/v1/messages`), and the federated `local-router/fallback-models` brain. Convergence: `local-router` becomes universal inference + PQC key protection for WTF and non-WTF apps; `wtf` keeps observability, bins, cluster coordination, and the federated shell.
- **Zero-config join** (2026-09-01): `wtf skill install` + one highly secure federated key must connect ANY agent on ANY machine autonomously — no manual configuration; all join tooling in-tree.
- **End-of-turn voice summary (TTS)** (2026-09-03, operator directive): every agent closes its turn with ONE fire-and-forget `cli-tts --prompt` call (kitten-tts-nano @ 1.8x, one ONNX session, quiet stdout; full contract in `.agents/skills/tts-cli/SKILL.md`). Prompt shape: concise change summary -> exactly one `Next step:` marker -> one sentence per master (adversarial/security, privacy, supply-chain, systems-architecture, reliability, governance, terminal-orchestration/SWE-bench, master-orchestrator, developer-experience). Transcripts auto-append to `AGENTS-TTS-COMMS.txt`.
- Any agent instructed to use, set up, join, or debug this system must load `.agents/skills/wtf-agent-hub/SKILL.md` first — the canonical zero-install operating guide (MCP wiring, signed curl fallback, operator CLI, multi-machine bring-up); `wtf-observability` is the legacy operator/CLI reference.

## Project Shape

Rust workspace (binary + lib crate `wtf`) implementing an observability hub (`wtf serve`) and an MCP stdio bridge (`wtf agent`) with zero external crates. Current release: **v0.15.2** (2026-09-03; 21 MCP tools; singular capability dashboard URL `/w/<capability>`; integrated Chat & Agent Orchestration Studio; paired Federated Shell `fed_shell.rs` with virtual `~/` cluster root, architecture LKGL tracking, and distributed OMP compute routing; R1 identity persistence in `identities.json` 0600; quiet heartbeats; dynamic context & multimodal fallback routing via local-router :11434; SWE-bench dual-engine fleet `trae-cli` + `mini`). Enrollment in two modes: `wtf enroll-token` mints one-time tokens (hashed, TTL); `wtf enroll --psk` signed handshake delivers the device key ML-KEM-768-sealed. All 108 unit tests and 14 e2e tests green.

Parent-owned here: repo workflow gates, task records (`.agents/tasks/`), PQC policy, operator preferences.

## Child DOX Index

- `src/llms.txt` — implementation tree: module map, crypto/HTTP/JSON/auth contracts, storage rules, verification commands.
- `docs/llms.txt` — operator/fleet documentation split (`FLEET.md` state inventory, `OPERATIONS.md` runbooks, `ROADMAP.md` refinement items). Root `llms.txt` stays the lean agent contract; human-facing state and runbooks live there.
- `tests/` — parent-owned for now (single e2e suite, no local conventions). Create `tests/llms.txt` if it grows its own rules.

## Distributed Skills

- `.agents/skills/wtf-agent-hub/SKILL.md` — the agent-facing connect + protocol skill (embedded in the binary; `wtf skill install` distributes it). Mirrored to ainish-coder.
- `.agents/skills/wtf-observability/SKILL.md` — operator/CLI + signed-curl fallback reference (legacy; agents use wtf-agent-hub).
- **Curated skill set (persisted selection, 2026-09-03):** this repo carries the 12 skills deployed by `ainish-coder --rules`: `code-security`, `graph-intelligence`, `model-add`, `model-remove`, `modern-prompting`, `pqc-secrets`, `pqc-signatures-security`, `production-security`, `provider-models-list`, `trae-mini-fleet`, `tts-cli`, `wtf-agent-hub`, plus the six GitNexus playbooks as standalone skills (`gitnexus-cli`, `gitnexus-debugging`, `gitnexus-exploring`, `gitnexus-guide`, `gitnexus-impact-analysis`, `gitnexus-refactoring`) Deselected packs (such as `llm-security`) are purged during deployment.
- PQC skills (`pqc-secrets`, `pqc-signatures-security`) are sourced from the ainish-coder repo and deployed by `ainish-coder --rules`.

## Chat integration — cross-system agent-to-agent lanes (v0.15.1, operator directive)

Federated chats ARE the cross-system agent-to-agent lanes. Contract:

1. **One chat = one project lane.** The scope label (`repo-a+repo-b@mac+win`)
   declares which repos on which machines the chat coordinates. Members join
   from any machine with the pairing key; every message is E2E-encrypted,
   replicated via the hub mesh, and visible decrypted to the operator's
   dashboard viewer.
2. **Agent-to-agent update flow.** Agent A (machine 1) posts progress via
   `session_send`/`comms_post`; Agent B (machine 2) polls via
   `session_read`/`comms_read` and executes the handed-off task through its
   own CLI (omp → hermes → fcc-claude). The repo chats on each machine are
   the discovery surface (`session_list {repo}`).
3. **Operator interjection.** The dashboard chat viewer exposes the same
   chat decrypted, plus a live terminal on the executor tmux session — the
   operator can type into either machine's agent session mid-conversation.
4. **Lifecycle.** Every connection opens its executor session on work start
   (`chat_session_lifecycle {action:"open"}`), closes or deletes it when
   done, and reconnects on a hung pane. Sessions are per-connection; bins
   are per-connection (dynamic ids from the device slot).
5. **Log hygiene.** Heartbeats and replication churn are quiet (presence
   only). The dashboard shows work; the ring + rotated log keep only
   troubleshooting-worthy signal.
6. **Cross-machine CLI helpers (windows-installed; promote to MCP later).**
   `wtf-ask --local "q"` runs the fallback chain locally and reports the
   lane. `wtf-ask-remote <session-id> "directive" [--wait N]` posts a
   directive into a chat via session_send and optionally polls
   session_read for the remote agent's reply — the message is the
   contract; the remote runtime (Windows/mac/Linux) is irrelevant.
